exec "$BIN" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# hotloops.sh must survive symbol tables that carry ELF visibility tokens:
# objdump -t prints hidden functions as "<addr> g F .text <size> .hidden
# <name>", which shifts the size field. The symbol-table parse must neither
# abort (gawk: "fatal: hexadecimal floating point constants require an
# exponent" on strtonum("0x.hidden")) nor mis-parse hidden FUNC symbols.
#
# Uses llvm-objdump (always prints the visibility token); skips cleanly
# when it or the build artifacts are absent.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

QEMU_BIN="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"

command -v llvm-objdump >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "SKIP: no llvm-objdump"; exit 0; }
[ -x "$QEMU_BIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: qemu not built"; exit 0; }
[ -f "$PLUGIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: hotloops plugin not built"; exit 0; }
[ -f "$ELF" ] || { echo "SKIP: vplat_hello.elf not built"; exit 0; }
llvm-objdump -t "$ELF" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '\.hidden' \
  || { echo "SKIP: fixture carries no .hidden symbols"; exit 0; }

err=$("$ROOT/QEMU/scripts/hotloops.sh" \
        --qemu "$QEMU_BIN" --plugin "$PLUGIN" --objdump llvm-objdump \
        --cpu "andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=512" \
        --no-optimize-rvv "$ELF" 2>&1 >/dev/null)
rc=$?

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[hotloops_hidden_syms]: hotloops.sh exited $rc"
  echo "$err"
  exit 1
fi
if printf '%s\n' "$err" | grep -q "awk:"; then
  echo "FAIL[hotloops_hidden_syms]: awk diagnostics leaked to stderr:"
  echo "$err"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS[hotloops_hidden_syms]"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# hotloops.sh LLM report contract: each loop block carries a ready hybrid
# pc window, `measure: --pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>`, derived from
# the loop's enclosing function. The loop's own pc_range is NOT a usable
# window (one-shot pc triggers fire on the first hit, so header..tail
# measures a single iteration); the function span covers every iteration
# and needs no objdump step from the user.
#
# Builds a tiny single-ret RVV kernel (vplat runtime), runs the detector,
# and checks the measure line against the toolchain's own nm/objdump as
# the oracle.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

QEMU_BIN="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so"

. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null || true
GCC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"
OBJDUMP="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"

[ -x "$QEMU_BIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: qemu not built"; exit 0; }
[ -f "$PLUGIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: hotloops plugin not built"; exit 0; }
[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "SKIP: no riscv toolchain"; exit 0; }
[ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime" ] || { echo "SKIP: vplat runtime not built"; exit 0; }

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t hotloops-measure.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

cat > "$TMP/vadd.c" <<'EOF'
#include <stdint.h>
#include <riscv_vector.h>
static int32_t a[64], b[64];
__attribute__((noinline)) static void vadd_kernel(void)
{
  for (int r = 0; r < 50; r++)
    for (int i = 0; i < 64;) {
      size_t vl = __riscv_vsetvl_e32m1((size_t) (64 - i));
      vint32m1_t va = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&a[i], vl);
      vint32m1_t vb = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&b[i], vl);
      __riscv_vse32_v_i32m1(&a[i], __riscv_vadd_vv_i32m1(va, vb, vl), vl);
      i += (int) vl;
    }
}
int main(void) { vadd_kernel(); return 0; }
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$ROOT/build/runtime" -specs=andesim.specs \
  "$TMP/vadd.c" -o "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: fixture build failed"; exit 1; }

REPORT=$("$ROOT/QEMU/scripts/hotloops.sh" \
           --qemu "$QEMU_BIN" --plugin "$PLUGIN" \
           --cpu "andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=512" \
           --min-iters 10 "$TMP/vadd.elf" 2>/dev/null)

echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "L1 \[hottest\]" \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no hottest loop reported"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }

MEASURE=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^measure:")
[ -n "$MEASURE" ] \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no measure: line in the report"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }

GOT_S=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-start 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
GOT_E=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')

# Oracle: the kernel's entry from nm; its return = the function's last
# instruction (single-epilogue at -O1; objdump flavors disagree on the
# `ret` vs `c.jr ra` spelling, so match by position, not mnemonic).
WANT_S=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$NM" "$TMP/vadd.elf" | awk '$3=="vadd_kernel"{print $1; exit}')")
WANT_E=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
  | sed -n '/<vadd_kernel>:/,/^$/p' | grep -E '^[ ]+[0-9a-f]+:' \
  | tail -1 | awk '{sub(":","",$1); print $1}')")

if [ "$GOT_S" != "$WANT_S" ] || [ "$GOT_E" != "$WANT_E" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: window $GOT_S..$GOT_E, want $WANT_S..$WANT_E"
  echo "$MEASURE"
  exit 1
fi

echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "Measure all of" \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: TL;DR carries no measure hint"; exit 1; }

# measure_loop: the loop's own first-pass window, [header, fall-through of
# the backward branch). pc-start = pc_range start; pc-end = the insn AFTER
# the branch in the disassembly (exact, works for compressed branches too).
ML=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^measure_loop:")
[ -n "$ML" ] \
  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no measure_loop: line"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }
ML_S=$(echo "$ML" | grep -o -- "--pc-start 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
ML_E=$(echo "$ML" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')

RANGE=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^pc_range:")
R_S=$(echo "$RANGE" | awk '{print $2}')
R_E=$(echo "$RANGE" | awk '{print $4}')
WANT_FT=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
  | awk -v tail="${R_E#0x}" 'f{sub(":","",$1); print $1; exit}
                             $1 == tail":"{f=1}')")

if [ "$ML_S" != "$R_S" ] || [ "$ML_E" != "$WANT_FT" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: measure_loop $ML_S..$ML_E, want $R_S..$WANT_FT"
  echo "$ML"
  exit 1
fi

echo "PASS[hotloops_measure]: measure = $GOT_S .. $GOT_E (function), measure_loop = $ML_S .. $ML_E (first pass)"

```sh

# ENTER = the entry marker encoding 5a002013 (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0);
# EXIT  = the LAST exit marker encoding 5a102013 (slti x0, x0, 0x5A1).
ENTER_PC=$("$OBJDUMP" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf \
            | awk '$2=="5a002013"{sub(/:$/,"",$1); print $1; exit}')
EXIT_PC=$("$OBJDUMP" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf \
            | awk '$2=="5a102013"{sub(/:$/,"",$1); pc=$1} END{print pc}')

echo "enter=$ENTER_PC  exit=$EXIT_PC"

# QEMU1 leg
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/share,size=134217728 \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=/tmp/q1.bin,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"

# vsim leg
"$VSIM_BIN" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf \
  --resume-from-qemu /tmp/q1.bin \
  --handoff-out /tmp/v.bin \
  --shared-mem-path /dev/shm/share \
  --shared-mem-size 134217728 \
  --hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC"
```

feat(hotloops): hot inner-loop detector plugin + driver subcommand

The libhotloops.so TCG plugin detects loops by watching for backward TB
transitions and ranks them by iteration count, so a fast QEMU run alone
reveals where a workload spends its time. build/hotloops is a standalone
C++20 tool that runs a bare-metal RISC-V ELF under that plugin and prints
the hottest loops as an LLM-ready Markdown fact sheet (function, source
file:line, PC range, RVV instruction listing). Each loop block carries a
ready measure: field -- the enclosing function's entry-to-ret PC window --
that pastes straight into an `--mode hybrid --trigger pc` run, so the user
picks a measurement window without hand-running objdump. The tool
auto-detects the QEMU binary, plugin, and CPU from the build, reads
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN from config.env for symbol resolution, batches addr2line
lookups over one pipe, and filters to RVV loops by default.

To support the measure: window, elf_syms gains symbolize() and fn_range()
-- the reverse lookup from a hot PC to its covering FUNC symbol and that
symbol's {entry, entry+size} span -- both sharing a new read_elf64_header
helper that also tidies resolve_pc. The plugin builds out-of-tree through
qemu_plugin/Makefile against the vendored qemu-plugin.h, alongside
libhybrid_handoff.so; the earlier shell prototype is kept verbatim as
scripts/hotloops.sh, the reference the plugin-smoke tests exercise.
